# requireNonFloat

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonFloat() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonFloat<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a value without a fractional part."
): T;
```

JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                  | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value without a fractional part."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a number with a fractional part excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                     |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a number with a fractional part. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonFloat(42); // => 42
requireNonFloat(1.0); // => 1.0
requireNonFloat(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonFloat(-0.1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
